newsitem.title: UK: EBRD looking at S.Korean, Taiwan bond issues.
newsitem.headline: EBRD looking at S.Korean, Taiwan bond issues.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Thursday it was considering South Korean and Taiwan bond issues.
Marcus Sedder, director of financial risk management, said that one tranche of the South Korean won issue would be for the domestic market and the other either a global or Eurobond.
He told Reuters the bank was looking at the equivalent of a $100 million issue which would be lead-managed by KDB Securities.
The EBRD is also in talks with the Taiwan authorities to try to solve tax issues before issuing a bond there. No amount has yet been decided.
Sedder said the bank was actively looking at other markets, including the Baltics, and it will probably later need zloty finance for a project.
Issues in its countries of operations -- such as recent ones in the Czech Republic and Slovakia -- tend to be short-term and more for arbitrage than for on-lending.
He said the bank could raise another 250 million Ecu over the rest of this year but was not forced to and would only go to the market if if could get the right pricing.
